Sprint 1 of inventory v1.0 fix plan in /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS. Three migrations + db:migrate + db:types.

Plan reference: /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/plans/inventory-page-lets-deep-enchanted-peach.md (Sprint 1 section).
Lessons mandatory: ~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md (RPC-only writes for audit tables, audit trigger pattern from supabase/migrations/s13_flash_inventory.sql line ~388).

## Migration 1 — `[ts]_inventory_p0_fixes.sql`

Goal: link `studio_ink_registry` to `inventory_items` so Brand/Color stop rendering "—". Enforce min_threshold >= 0.

```sql
-- Add FK + index
ALTER TABLE studio_ink_registry
  ADD COLUMN item_id uuid REFERENCES inventory_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_studio_ink_registry_item_id ON studio_ink_registry(item_id);

-- Backfill: match on (studio_id, LOWER(brand), LOWER(color)) for ink-category items
UPDATE studio_ink_registry r
SET item_id = i.id
FROM inventory_items i
WHERE i.studio_id = r.studio_id
  AND LOWER(TRIM(i.brand)) = LOWER(TRIM(r.brand))
  AND LOWER(TRIM(i.color)) = LOWER(TRIM(r.color))
  AND i.category = 'ink'
  AND r.item_id IS NULL;

-- Constraint
ALTER TABLE inventory_items
  ADD CONSTRAINT inventory_items_min_threshold_nonneg CHECK (min_threshold >= 0);
```

After writing: report rows backfilled vs unmatched (so we know how many need manual link in admin panel).

Inspect existing studio_ink_registry RLS policies to ensure they cover the new item_id column join. If a cross-table consistency check is missing, add a row-level CHECK trigger that ensures `item_id IS NULL OR (SELECT studio_id FROM inventory_items WHERE id = NEW.item_id) = NEW.studio_id`.

## Migration 2 — `[ts]_inventory_low_stock_trigger.sql`

Auto-create stock_alerts row when current_stock crosses below min_threshold; auto-resolve when stock returns at/above min.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_inventory_low_stock_handler()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Only fire when min_threshold > 0
  IF NEW.min_threshold > 0 AND NEW.current_stock < NEW.min_threshold THEN
    INSERT INTO stock_alerts (studio_id, item_id, created_at)
    VALUES (NEW.studio_id, NEW.id, now())
    ON CONFLICT (studio_id, item_id) WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL DO NOTHING;
  ELSIF NEW.current_stock >= NEW.min_threshold THEN
    UPDATE stock_alerts
       SET acknowledged_at = now(), notes = COALESCE(notes, '') || ' [auto-resolved]'
     WHERE item_id = NEW.id AND acknowledged_at IS NULL;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_inventory_low_stock
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF current_stock, min_threshold ON inventory_items
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION fn_inventory_low_stock_handler();
```

Inspect actual `stock_alerts` schema first. The partial unique index `(studio_id, item_id) WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL` may not exist; create it if needed for ON CONFLICT to work, or restructure with SELECT-then-INSERT in the function.

## Migration 3 — `[ts]_inventory_audit_trigger.sql`

Audit trigger on inventory_items, inventory_movements, purchase_orders, stock_alerts. Pattern: read supabase/migrations/s13_flash_inventory.sql around line 388 first to match shape.

Throttle: skip when `pg_trigger_depth() > 1` to avoid cascade flood from bulk imports / parent triggers.

## After writing all 3 migrations

1. Run `pnpm db:migrate` (verify clean apply, no errors).
2. Run `pnpm db:types` (regenerates lib/supabase/types.ts — never hand-edit).
3. Smoke test via psql: insert an item with current_stock=2, min_threshold=5 → confirm stock_alerts row appears. Update current_stock=10 → confirm acknowledged_at populates.

## Report back

- Migration filenames written.
- Rows backfilled in studio_ink_registry vs unmatched count.
- Any RLS policy adjustments made.
- Confirmation `pnpm db:types` regenerated cleanly.
- Smoke test outcome.

11	# InkOS Build Lessons
12	
13	## 1. Recurring Sage Findings — Systematic Pipeline Weaknesses
14	
15	### 1A. RPC Parameter Mismatches (Dato writes RPC, Koda writes route with different params)
16	
17	Appeared in Sprint 5 (C1: camelCase `submissionId` vs snake_case `submission_id` in consent PDF job), Sprint 6 (C1: `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`; C2: `accept_team_invite` missing `artist_id` and `commission_default_pct` in return shape), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), and Sprint 8 (S8#1: `set_artist_tax_info` param mismatch). Root cause: Dato writes the migration defining the RPC signature, Koda writes the API route consuming it, and neither verifies the other's contract. The hand-written `lib/supabase/types.ts` masks the drift because TypeScript trusts whatever is manually typed. **Prevention rule:** Before Koda writes any route that calls an RPC, the RPC's exact parameter names and return fields must be extracted from the migration SQL into a shared TypeScript interface. If Dato and Koda run in parallel, the contract must be defined in the design spec as a shared interface BEFORE either starts coding.
18	
19	### 1B. Column Name Drift (migration says X, types say Y, code says Z)
20	
21	Appeared in Sprint 1 (C3: `locations` migration missing `zip`/`phone` that types declared), Sprint 3 (C2: `sort_order` column missing from migration but code referenced it), Sprint 6 (C3: `studio_members.last_active_at` not in migration but in types), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), Sprint 8-12 audit (S11#8: `status` column on `marketing_campaigns` missing, S12#12: `payroll_items` table referenced but doesn't exist). Root cause: `lib/supabase/types.ts` was hand-edited throughout the build instead of regenerated from the actual DB schema. **Prevention rule:** Never hand-edit the types file. After every Dato migration, run `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet (as in InkOS), maintain a strict convention: Dato writes the migration, Dato updates types to exactly match, and Koda does NOT touch the types file. Any column referenced in code must exist in the migration first.
22	
23	### 1C. `asChild` Violations on base-nova
24	
25	Every Sage audit checked for `asChild` usage on base-nova (shadcn/ui's `@base-ui-components/react`) components. In InkOS this passed cleanly because it was caught early (Sprint 1 scan), but the automated grep for `asChild` was added to every single audit because this is a known recurring problem across Boldteq builds. **Rule:** All components from base-nova use the `render` prop pattern, never `asChild`. This must be in every project's ESLint config as a custom rule or at minimum in the Sage automated scan.
26	
27	### 1D. Missing Rate Limits on GET Endpoints
28	
29	Sprint 1 (M1: auth rate limits architecturally impossible), Sprint 6 (public invite route needed rate limit), Sprint 8-12 combined audit (cross-sprint #17: payroll GET routes missing rate limits). Koda consistently forgets rate limits on read routes, treating them as "safe." But unbounded GETs enable enumeration, scraping, and DoS. **Rule:** Every API route, GET or POST, must import and call either `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before any DB query. Sage scans for routes missing rate-limit calls.
30	
31	### 1E. `onValueChange` Null Guards for base-ui Select
32	
33	Not specific to InkOS (passed here) but flagged as a check item in every audit. When base-ui Select fires `onValueChange`, the value can be `null` on deselect. Without a guard, the handler crashes or sends null to the API. **Rule:** Every `onValueChange` handler must check `if (value === null) return` before processing.
34	
35	### 1F. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` Violations
36	
37	Sprint 4 build report (item #2): interface optionals needed `| undefined` suffix. Throughout the build, Koda hit TypeScript errors where `{ field?: string }` doesn't accept `undefined` under strict optional property types. **Rule:** Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, always declare optional fields as `field?: string | undefined` in interfaces. Or better: use Zod schema inference (`z.infer<typeof Schema>`) which handles this automatically.
38	
39	### 1G. Feature Gate Key Mismatches
40	
41	Sprint 7 (C1): the plans JSONB in the billing migration used `commission_splits` but all code used `commissions`. Today's static `requireFeature()` compares plan order (not JSONB keys), so it accidentally worked. But if anyone switches to the RPC-based `requireFeatureRpc()` (which reads JSONB), all gates 403. **Rule:** Define all feature gate keys in a single `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` constant. Both the migration seed data and the `requireFeature()` callers import from this file. Drift is a compile error instead of a runtime surprise.
42	
43	### 1H. Public Routes Using Session Client Instead of Anon
44	
45	Sprint 5 (C6, C7): public consent pages imported `createClient` from `@/lib/supabase/server` (session-cookie client) instead of `createPublicClient`. Functional today (RPC grants to anon) but leaks the logged-in user's session into a public route. **Rule:** Every route under `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, or `/api/public/` must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`. Sage grepping for `createClient` in public routes is now a mandatory scan.
46	
47	### 1I. `unstable_cache` Capturing Authenticated Clients
48	
49	Sprint 7 (M3): `unstable_cache(async () => supabase.rpc(...))` captured the first caller's authenticated client. Subsequent requests within the cache TTL reuse the first caller's JWT. **Rule:** Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` calls in `unstable_cache` when the supabase client is session-scoped. Cache the RESULT of the RPC call (a plain object), not the client invocation. Or just don't use `unstable_cache` for authenticated data -- it's not worth the footgun.
50	
51	## 2. Sprint Velocity Patterns — What Worked for Parallel Execution
52	
53	### 2A. Dato + Vega in Parallel (No Dependency)
54	
55	Dato writes the migration (schema, RPCs, RLS, triggers) while Vega writes the design spec (UI layout, component hierarchy, interaction patterns). These have zero dependencies. Starting them in parallel saves 2-4 hours per sprint. Koda then consumes BOTH outputs to build the API routes and UI.
56	
57	### 2B. Sage Audit in Background While Next Sprint Starts
58	
59	After Koda delivers a sprint, Sage audits the output while Dato and Vega start on the next sprint. The next sprint's Koda build can begin on features that don't overlap with the audit scope. This pipeline parallelism was critical for shipping 13 sprints in 2 days. Exception: if Sage's audit is BLOCK severity, the fix Koda must run before proceeding.
60	
61	### 2C. Fix Koda + Build Koda Can Run in Parallel If File Scopes Don't Overlap
62	
63	When Sage flags fixes in Sprint N, a "fix Koda" agent addresses those while a "build Koda" agent starts Sprint N+1's non-overlapping files. This worked well when Sprint 3 fixes (client CRM) ran alongside Sprint 4 scaffold (billing). Does NOT work when the fix touches shared infrastructure like `lib/supabase/types.ts` or `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
64	
65	### 2D. API 500 Errors Recovered by Checking Partial State
66	
67	When a sprint's build partially failed (e.g., missing column caused a 500), Rex dispatched a fix agent that first checked what was already built and correct, then surgically fixed only the broken parts. Avoids the temptation to rewrite entire files.
68	
69	### 2E. Batch Sage Audits Are Worse Than Per-Sprint Audits
70	
71	Sprints 8-12 were batched into one combined Sage audit. This found 4 critical issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. 73	## 3. Architecture Decisions That Proved Right
74	
75	### 3A. RPC-Only Writes for Audit-Critical Tables
76	
77	`consent_form_submissions` has zero direct-write RLS policies -- all writes go through `submit_consent_form` RPC. `commission_records` same pattern. This means: (a) business logic (snapshot creation, audit hash, penalty generation) can't be bypassed; (b) the RPC is the single source of truth for mutation semantics; (c) RLS stays simple (just read policies). **Apply to:** Any table where data integrity is a legal or financial obligation (consent, pay, billing, audit logs).
78	
79	### 3B. `EXCLUDE USING gist` for Booking Conflicts
80	
81	The `bookings_artist_no_overlap` exclusion constraint catches double-bookings at the DB level. Every write path (API route, public RPC, admin override) that creates/moves a booking is automatically protected. Without this, every write path would need its own conflict-check query, and one would inevitably be missed. Effort to set up: 5 lines of SQL. Effort saved: hours of bug-hunting. **Apply to:** Any domain with time-range conflicts (schedules, reservations, resource allocation).
82	
83	### 3C. `GENERATED ALWAYS` Columns for Computed Values
84	
85	`bookings.end_at` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`. This means `end_at` can never drift from `scheduled_at + duration`. No code path can accidentally set a wrong `end_at`. Sage verified this by grepping for `end_at` in INSERT/UPDATE payloads -- zero hits. **Apply to:** Any column that's a deterministic function of other columns (totals, dates, durations).
86	
87	### 3D. Feature Gate Server-Enforced + UI-Hidden (Dual Enforcement)
88	
89	Every gated feature has: (1) `requireFeature(plan, 'key')` in the API route that returns 403, AND (2) `featureKey` in the sidebar nav-config that hides the link AND (3) `<UpgradeGate>` component that shows a blur overlay. Three layers means a user can never reach a paid feature through URL manipulation, deep linking, or API probing. **Apply to:** Every SaaS with tiered plans.
90	
91	### 3E. Worker-Only for Expensive Operations
92	
93	AI design generation (Claude + DALL-E pipeline), PDF generation (react-pdf/renderer), and low-stock email alerts all run in BullMQ workers, never in API routes. This prevents: request timeouts, memory pressure on the web process, and blocking other requests. **Apply to:** Any operation that takes >5s or uses >100MB memory.
94

The types file was 3000+ lines of manually maintained TypeScript that drifted from reality. **Fix for future builds:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after every migration. The actual `proxy.ts` file existed and worked, but new contributors would look for `middleware.ts` and not find it. **Rule:** On every Next.js major version, verify the middleware filename convention. 109	## 5. Koda Recurring Type Fix Patterns
110	
111	### 5A. `Object.assign` Bypass for Supabase `RejectExcessProperties`
112	
113	When Supabase client's `.update()` or `.insert()` rejects unknown properties, Koda used `Object.assign(base, { extra_field: value })` to sneak in properties not in the TypeScript type. Sprint 3 (C2): this was used to write a `sort_order` column that didn't exist. The `Object.assign` defeated TypeScript's protection and the write silently no-oped. **Rule:** NEVER use `Object.assign` to build Supabase mutation payloads. If a field isn't in the type, it shouldn't be in the mutation. If it SHOULD be there, fix the type first.
114	
115	### 5B. `unknown as TableInsert` Cast Pattern
116	
117	When the Supabase generated types don't match what code needs to insert, Koda cast `payload as unknown as Database['public']['Tables']['x']['Insert']`. This bypasses all type checking. Acceptable ONLY when the mismatch is between the generated type and the actual DB schema (which happens when types aren't regenerated). **Rule:** Fix the root cause (regenerate types) instead of casting.
118	
119	### 5C. `Resolver<FormValues>` Explicit Cast for react-hook-form
120	
121	react-hook-form's `zodResolver()` returns a type that doesn't exactly match `Resolver<T>` under strict settings. Koda added explicit `as Resolver<FormValues>` casts. This is a known library typing issue and the cast is safe. **Rule:** Acceptable -- document in codebase as a known workaround.
122	
123	### 5D. `render` Not `asChild` on Every base-nova Component
124	
125	Covered in 1C above. Every component from `@base-ui-components/react` uses `render` prop, never `asChild`. Koda initially used `asChild` (Radix habit), caught in Sprint 1, never repeated.
126	
127	### 5E. `.slice(0, 10)` Instead of `.split('T')[0]` for ISO Date Extraction
128	
129	Under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `.split('T')[0]` returns `string | undefined` because TypeScript doesn't know the array has a first element. `.slice(0, 10)` returns `string` always. **Rule:** For extracting the date portion of an ISO string, use `.slice(0, 10)`. It's type-safe and doesn't require a non-null assertion.

131	## 6. Dodo Payments Integration Gotchas
132	
133	### 6A. `standardwebhooks` Spec (Not Plain HMAC)
134	
135	Sprint 4 (C1): Dodo webhooks use the `standardwebhooks` library, NOT a plain HMAC. The signing payload is `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`, the secret is base64-decoded (strip `whsec_` prefix), and the signature header format is `v1,base64sig`. A plain `createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')` will NEVER match. **Rule:** Use `import { Webhook } from 'standardwebhooks'` and call `wh.verify(rawBody, headers)`. The idempotency key is the `webhook-id` header, not a body-level `event_id` field (which Dodo doesn't send).
136	
137	### 6B. `customer: {customer_id}` Object Format
138	
139	Dodo SDK v2 `subscriptions.create` and `payments.create` take `customer: CustomerRequest` object (with `customer_id` field inside), NOT a top-level `customer_id` string. **Rule:** Always wrap: `{ customer: { customer_id: dodoCustomerId } }`.
140	
141	### 6C. `billing: {country}` Required on Checkout
142	
143	Every Dodo checkout call requires a `billing: { country: 'US' }` field. Without it, the API returns a 400 that's hard to debug. **Rule:** Always include `billing: { country }` in checkout creation.
144	
145	### 6D. `return_url` Not `success_url/cancel_url`
146	
147	Dodo uses a single `return_url` for post-checkout redirect, not separate `success_url` and `cancel_url` like Stripe. **Rule:** Pass `return_url` pointing to a confirmation page that checks the subscription/payment status.
148	
149	### 6E. Portal Method Returns `{link}`
150	
151	`dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(customerId, { return_url })` returns `{ link: string }`, not a full URL string. Access via `result.link`. **Rule:** Destructure: `const { link } = await dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(...)`.
152	
153	### 6F. Lazy Proxy Init for SDK Client
154	
155	Both `lib/dodo/client.ts` and `lib/queue.ts` were constructing SDK clients at module evaluation time. During `pnpm build`, env vars aren't available, causing a crash. Fixed with a lazy proxy pattern that defers construction until first use. **Rule:** Any SDK client that reads env vars at construction time must use lazy initialization. Pattern:
156	
157	```ts
158	let _client: DodoPayments | null = null
159	function getClient(): DodoPayments {
160	  if (!_client) _client = new DodoPayments({ token: process.env.DODO_API_KEY! })
161	  return _client
162	}
163	```

176	
177	The #1 integration bug category (1A above) is Dato and Koda disagreeing on RPC parameter names and return shapes. Fix: in the design spec, define each RPC as a TypeScript interface:

184	  p_submission_data: Json

196	### 7D. Create `.env.local.template` That Can Be Copied in One Command
197	
198	InkOS accumulated 30+ env vars across 13 sprints. Each new env var was mentioned in a build report but not collected in one place until late. **Rule:** Maintain a `.env.local.template` from Sprint 0 that's updated every sprint. New developer setup: `cp .env.local.template .env.local` then fill in secrets.

200	### 7E. Storage RLS Must Be Checked Per-Bucket, Per-Sprint
201	
202	Sprint 1 fixed storage RLS for `studio-assets`. Sprint 2 added `design-assets` bucket without copying the RLS pattern. Sprint 2 Sage caught it. Sprint 5 added `consent-forms` bucket -- same risk. **Rule:** Every time a Dato migration creates a new storage bucket, Sage must verify that SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies exist with folder-prefix tenant checks. Add to the automated scan.
203	
204	### 7F. Admin Routes Must Use Service-Role Client After Platform Admin Gate
205	
206	Sprint 4 (C2): All admin billing routes used the session client, so RLS restricted the platform admin to their own studio's data. Admin routes see zero cross-tenant data. **Rule:** After verifying `is_platform_admin`, switch to `createServiceRoleClient()`. The admin gate is authorization; service-role bypasses RLS for the cross-tenant query.
207	
208	### 7G. CSV/Export Routes Must Sanitize for Formula Injection
209	
210	Sprint 3 (C3): `Papa.unparse` does not escape cells starting with `= + - @ \t \r`. Any export feature is a CWE-1236 vector. **Rule:** Every CSV export must wrap cell values in a `sanitiseCsvCell()` function that prefixes dangerous characters with `'`. Add this to the shared `lib/utils.ts` in the starter template.
211	
212	### 7H. Delete Operations Must Verify Affected Row Count
213	
214	Sprint 3 (M2): Supabase `.delete()` returns `{ error: null }` even when RLS denies the delete (zero rows affected). The UI optimistically removes the item, but on reload it's back. **Rule:** Always use `.delete({ count: 'exact' })` and check `count === 0` to return 403/404. Apply to every DELETE handler.
215	
216	### 7I. Mutation Routes Must Use RPCs When RPCs Exist
217	
218	Sprint 6 (M2): Dato wrote `change_member_role` and `deactivate_member` RPCs with last-owner protection and audit logging. Koda's API routes bypassed them with direct `.update()` calls, losing all the safety logic. **Rule:** If a SECURITY DEFINER RPC exists for a mutation, the API route MUST call it. Direct `.update()` or `.insert()` bypasses triggers, audit logging, and business rules baked into the RPC.

393	### M4. Orphan-comm antipattern in auto-reply RPC
394	
395	`enqueue_auto_reply` RPC inserted a `client_communications` row with `status='queued'` AND stamped `conversations.last_auto_reply_at` BEFORE checking whether the dispatch channel was supported. 397	**Rule:** State-changing RPCs that depend on external dispatchability must gate on capability BEFORE writing state. Order:
398	1. Validate the channel is supported (env check, config row, capability table).
399	2. If not → return early with a clear "channel_unsupported" status, write NOTHING.
400	3. Only after capability check → insert queued row + stamp `last_*_at`.

402	Equivalent rule for any "enqueue + stamp + dispatch" flow: capability → write → dispatch. Never write → discover-unsupported → leak.

404	### M5. Webhook returns 200 when config is missing
405	
406	The Meta (Instagram/Messenger) webhook route returned 200 silently when `META_APP_SECRET` was unset. Meta treats 200 as successful delivery and never retries — messages were dropped with zero observable signal.
407	
408	**Rule:** Webhook config errors return **503 Service Unavailable**, not 200. 503 signals "provider, retry later, ops will fix this." The provider keeps retrying on its schedule, and the missing-config error shows up in logs, dashboards, and alerts.
409	
410	Pattern for every webhook route:
411	```ts
412	const secret = process.env.META_APP_SECRET
413	if (!secret) {
414	  logger.error({ webhook: 'meta' }, 'META_APP_SECRET not configured')
415	  return new Response('Webhook not configured', { status: 503 })
416	}
417	```
418	
419	Apply to ALL webhook routes: Dodo, Meta, Twilio, Resend, any future provider. The only 200 a webhook returns is after successful processing (or successful idempotent-replay detection).

422	
423	`workers/jobs/send-scheduled-message.ts` had an early `throw new Error('scheduled time not reached')` when the job was processed before its target time. BullMQ counts every throw as a failed attempt — 3 throws and the job is dead-lettered, even though the "failure" was entirely expected (the scheduler just has fuzzy timing).
424	
425	**Rule:** In BullMQ worker bodies, NEVER throw for expected transient states (not-yet-time, rate-limit-cooldown, external-service-busy-retry-later). Use one of:
426	- `return` (mark job complete, success) — appropriate if another mechanism will re-schedule.
427	- `await job.moveToDelayed(nextRunAt.getTime())` — push the job back to the delayed queue until the target time, doesn't count as a failure.
428	- `throw new UnrecoverableError(...)` — explicit dead-letter, skip remaining retries.
429	
430	`throw` is for genuine, unexpected failure. Every retry budget is finite; burning it on clock skew is a waste.

432	### M7. Template rendering must match DEFAULT_TEMPLATES token set exactly
433	
434	Initial `enqueue_auto_reply` RPC rendered only 3 tokens (`{{studio_name}}`, `{{client_first_name}}`, `{{booking_link}}`) but `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` shipped with 5 tokens including `{{portfolio_link}}` and `{{aftercare_pdf_link}}`. A follow-up migration was required to add the missing REPLACE chain + a defensive `REGEXP_REPLACE` strip for unresolved `{{anything}}` tokens (so broken templates don't leak raw Liquid to clients).
435	
436	**Rule:** When designing any templated-string RPC:
437	1. Enumerate the FULL token set in the design spec before Dato writes the migration.
438	2. The RPC's REPLACE chain must cover EVERY token the UI/seed data exposes.
439	3. Add a defensive tail: `REGEXP_REPLACE(rendered, '\{\{[^}]+\}\}', '', 'g')` to strip any unresolved tokens rather than leaking them.
440	4. If the token set changes, a migration is required — treat the template contract like an API contract.
441	
442	Canonical pattern: keep token definitions in a single shared source (`lib/messaging/template-tokens.ts`), and reference them from both the seed data and the RPC's REPLACE chain generator.
443	
444	### M8. `.single()` throws `PGRST116` on upsert with no returned rows
445	
446	`seedDefaultTemplates()` used `.upsert(...).select('id').single()`. When the upsert was a no-op (row already existed with same values), Supabase returned 0 rows, and `.single()` threw `PGRST116 — Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object`. The seed function crashed on the happy-path second run.
447	
448	**Rule:** In seed/idempotent functions, use `.maybeSingle()` (returns `null` instead of throwing) and explicitly guard the `23505` unique-violation code if you're using plain `.insert()` with `ON CONFLICT`. Pattern:
449	```ts
450	const { data, error } = await supabase
451	  .from('message_templates')
452	  .upsert(payload, { onConflict: 'studio_id,kind' })
453	  .select('id')
454	  .maybeSingle()
455	
456	if (error && error.code !== '23505') throw error
457	```
458	
459	`.single()` is only for queries where exactly one row is guaranteed (e.g., primary-key lookups after a verified insert).

506	### M11. Supabase Realtime presence channels — typing + viewing indicator pattern
507	
508	Canonical pattern for "who is looking at / typing in this conversation right now":
509	
510	```ts
511	// hooks/messaging/use-conversation-presence.ts
512	const channel = supabase.channel(`presence:conversation:${conversationId}`, {
513	  config: { presence: { key: userId } },
514	})
515	
516	channel
517	  .on('presence', { event: 'sync' }, () => {
518	    const state = channel.presenceState<{ userId: string; userName: string; state: 'viewing' | 'typing'; ts: number }>()
519	    setPresent(
520	      Object.values(state)
521	        .flat()
522	        .filter(p => p.userId !== currentUserId), // exclude self
523	    )
524	  })
525	  .subscribe(async (status) => {
526	    if (status !== 'SUBSCRIBED') return
527	    await channel.track({ userId, userName, state: 'viewing', ts: Date.now() })
528	  })
529	
530	// Typing updates — throttled
531	const trackTyping = throttle(
532	  () => channel.track({ userId, userName, state: 'typing', ts: Date.now() }),
533	  TYPING_THROTTLE_MS,
534	)
535	
536	// Cleanup on unmount — MUST call removeChannel
537	return () => void supabase.removeChannel(channel)
538	```
539	
540	**Rules:**
541	- Channel key: `presence:{entity_type}:{entity_id}` — stable, namespaced, predictable.
542	- Presence `key` = `userId` — deduplicates a user's own multiple tabs (only latest state sticks).
543	- ALWAYS exclude the current user from the rendered list (`p.userId !== currentUserId`).
544	- Throttle `track()` calls for typing — 1 per `TYPING_THROTTLE_MS` (e.g., 2000ms). Every keystroke is a network round-trip otherwise.
545	- ALWAYS clean up with `supabase.removeChannel(channel)` on unmount. Leaked channels accumulate and eventually exceed Realtime's per-project channel cap.
546	- Presence state is NOT persisted — it's ephemeral. For "last seen at" use a `user_presence` table updated via throttled server action.

Sage passed (grep-based scans saw the file on disk), but Bolt's pre-deploy check caught it: Railway would deploy from the commit, and the commit didn't contain the worker. 9	## 1. MIGRATION SAFETY
10	
11	### Naming Convention
12	```
13	supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql
14	```
15	Example: `20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql`
16	
17	### Zero-Downtime Migration Rules
18	
19	**SAFE (no lock, no downtime):**
20	```sql
21	-- Add nullable column
22	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN description text;
23	
24	-- Add column with default (Postgres 11+ is instant)
25	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
26	
27	-- Create index concurrently (doesn't lock table)
28	CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
29	
30	-- Create new table
31	CREATE TABLE project_tags (...);
32	
33	-- Add foreign key (NOT VALID skips validation of existing rows)
34	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user
35	  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) NOT VALID;
36	-- Then validate separately (lighter lock):
37	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_user;
38	```
39	
40	**DANGEROUS (locks table, causes downtime):**
41	```sql
42	-- ❌ Adding NOT NULL to existing column without default
43	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN description SET NOT NULL;
44	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Add check constraint
45	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null
46	  CHECK (description IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;
47	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null;
48	
49	-- ❌ Renaming a column (breaks all queries referencing old name)
50	ALTER TABLE projects RENAME COLUMN name TO title;
51	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Expand-migrate-contract pattern
52	-- 1. Add new column: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN title text;
53	-- 2. Backfill: UPDATE projects SET title = name WHERE title IS NULL;
54	-- 3. Switch app code to read/write title
55	-- 4. Drop old: ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN name;
56	
57	-- ❌ Changing column type
58	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN price TYPE numeric;
59	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: New column + backfill + swap
60	
61	-- ❌ CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY
62	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user ON projects(user_id);
63	-- ✅ Always: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
64	```
65	
66	### Migration Rollback Strategy
67	
68	Every migration file should have a corresponding rollback comment:
69	```sql
70	-- Migration: 20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql
71	-- Rollback: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS projects CASCADE;
72	
73	CREATE TABLE projects (
74	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
75	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
76	  name text NOT NULL,
77	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
78	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
79	);
80	```
81	
82	If a migration fails mid-flight:
83	1. Check what was applied: `SELECT * FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;`
84	2. Manually fix the state or apply the rollback SQL
85	3. Never delete a migration file that's been applied — create a new migration to undo it

89	## 2. RLS (Row Level Security) — COMPLETE PATTERNS
90	
91	### Pattern A: User-owned data
92	```sql
93	ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
94	
95	-- Users see only their own projects
96	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own" ON projects
97	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
98	
99	CREATE POLICY "users_insert_own" ON projects
100	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
101	
102	CREATE POLICY "users_update_own" ON projects
103	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id)
104	  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
105	
106	CREATE POLICY "users_delete_own" ON projects
107	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
108	```
109	
110	### Pattern B: Team/org-scoped data
111	```sql
112	-- Members of an org can see org data
113	CREATE POLICY "org_members_select" ON projects
114	  FOR SELECT USING (
115	    org_id IN (
116	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
117	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
118	    )
119	  );
120	
121	-- Only admins can delete
122	CREATE POLICY "org_admins_delete" ON projects
123	  FOR DELETE USING (
124	    org_id IN (
125	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
126	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'admin'
127	    )
128	  );
129	```
130	
131	### Pattern C: Public read, authenticated write
132	```sql
133	CREATE POLICY "anyone_select" ON blog_posts
134	  FOR SELECT USING (published = true);
135	
136	CREATE POLICY "authors_insert" ON blog_posts
137	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = author_id);
138	
139	CREATE POLICY "authors_update" ON blog_posts
140	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = author_id);

143	### Pattern D: Service role bypass (for webhooks, background jobs)
144	```sql
145	-- Service role bypasses RLS by default in Supabase
146	-- But if you WANT policies for service role:
147	CREATE POLICY "service_role_all" ON projects
148	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
149	```

152	### RLS Performance Rules
153	```sql
154	-- ❌ SLOW: Subquery in every row check
155	CREATE POLICY "slow_policy" ON data
156	  FOR SELECT USING (
157	    user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM permissions WHERE ...)
158	  );
159	
160	-- ✅ FAST: Use a security definer function + cache
161	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_org_ids()
162	RETURNS uuid[] AS $$
163	  SELECT COALESCE(
164	    array_agg(org_id),
165	    '{}'::uuid[]
166	  )
167	  FROM org_members
168	  WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
169	$$ LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE;
170	
171	CREATE POLICY "fast_org_policy" ON data
172	  FOR SELECT USING (org_id = ANY(auth.user_org_ids()));
173	
174	-- Index to support the function
175	CREATE INDEX idx_org_members_user_id ON org_members(user_id);
176	```

245	CREATE TABLE audit_log (
246	  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
247	  table_name text NOT NULL,
248	  record_id uuid NOT NULL,
249	  action text NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')),
250	  old_data jsonb,

263	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$

314	
315	### When to Create Indexes
316	```sql
317	-- Rule: Index every column used in WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY, or RLS policy
318	
319	-- Foreign keys (ALWAYS index these — Postgres doesn't auto-index FKs)
320	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);

381	## 5. SUPABASE REALTIME SUBSCRIPTIONS
382	
383	### Pattern: Subscribe to table changes (React)
384	```tsx
385	'use client'
386	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
387	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'
388	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
389	
390	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
391	
392	export function useRealtimeProjects(userId: string) {
393	  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([])
394	  const supabase = createClient()
395	
396	  useEffect(() => {
397	    // Initial fetch
398	    supabase
399	      .from('projects')
400	      .select('*')
401	      .eq('user_id', userId)
402	      .then(({ data }) => {
403	        if (data) setProjects(data)
404	      })
405	
406	    // Subscribe to changes
407	    const channel = supabase
408	      .channel('projects-changes')
409	      .on(
410	        'postgres_changes',
411	        {
412	          event: '*',
413	          schema: 'public',
414	          table: 'projects',
415	          filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}`,
416	        },
417	        (payload) => {
418	          if (payload.eventType === 'INSERT') {
419	            setProjects(prev => [...prev, payload.new as Project])
420	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'UPDATE') {
421	            setProjects(prev =>
422	              prev.map(p => p.id === (payload.new as Project).id ? payload.new as Project : p)
423	            )
424	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'DELETE') {
425	            setProjects(prev =>
426	              prev.filter(p => p.id !== (payload.old as Project).id)
427	            )
428	          }
429	        }
430	      )
431	      .subscribe()
432	
433	    // CRITICAL: Cleanup on unmount

436	    }
437	  }, [userId])

443	### Realtime Rules
444	1. **Always clean up subscriptions** on component unmount (`removeChannel`)
445	2. **Use filters** (`filter: 'user_id=eq.xxx'`) to reduce payload — never subscribe to entire table
446	3. **RLS applies to Realtime** — users only receive changes they're authorized to see
447	4. **Enable Realtime per table** in Supabase Dashboard → Database → Replication
448	5. **Max channels:** ~100 per client connection. Pool carefully.
449	6. **Don't use Realtime for large datasets** — it sends full row payloads. For high-volume, use polling + React Query.

459	## 6. SUPABASE EDGE FUNCTIONS
460	
461	### When to Use Edge Functions vs API Routes
462	- **Edge Functions:** Low-latency global execution, Deno runtime, ~50ms cold start. Use for: lightweight webhooks, image transforms, geolocation-based logic.
463	- **Next.js API Routes (on Railway):** Full Node.js, access to BullMQ/Redis, no cold start. Use for: complex business logic, background jobs, AI inference, heavy computation.
464	
465	**Default to API Routes.** Edge Functions only when latency from a specific region matters.
466	
467	### Edge Function Structure
468	```
469	supabase/functions/
470	  my-function/
471	    index.ts        # Entry point
472	    _shared/        # Shared code between functions
473	      cors.ts
474	      supabase.ts
475	```
476	
477	### Edge Function Template
478	```ts
479	// supabase/functions/my-function/index.ts
480	import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2'
481	
482	const corsHeaders = {
483	  'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
484	  'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type',
485	}
486	
487	Deno.serve(async (req: Request) => {
488	  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
489	    return new Response('ok', { headers: corsHeaders })
490	  }
491	
492	  try {
493	    const supabase = createClient(
494	      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
495	      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!
496	    )
497	
498	    const { data, error } = await supabase
499	      .from('projects')
500	      .select('*')
501	      .limit(10)
502	
503	    if (error) throw error
504	
505	    return new Response(JSON.stringify(data), {
506	      headers: { ...corsHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
507	    })
508	  } catch (err) {
509	    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: err.message }), {
510	      status: 500,
511	      headers: { ...corsHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
512	    })
513	  }
514	})
515	```
516	
517	### Deploy Edge Functions
518	```bash
519	supabase functions deploy my-function --project-ref $PROJECT_REF
520	```

524	## 7. SCHEMA DESIGN PATTERNS
525	
526	### Standard Table Template
527	```sql
528	CREATE TABLE public.{table_name} (
529	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
530	  -- ownership
531	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
532	  -- OR for org-scoped:
533	  -- org_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
534	
535	  -- data columns here
536	
537	  -- timestamps (EVERY table gets these)
538	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
539	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
540	);
541	
542	-- RLS (EVERY table)
543	ALTER TABLE public.{table_name} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
544	
545	-- Policies (minimum: SELECT + INSERT for owner)
546	CREATE POLICY "{table}_select" ON public.{table_name}
547	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
548	CREATE POLICY "{table}_insert" ON public.{table_name}
549	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
550	CREATE POLICY "{table}_update" ON public.{table_name}
551	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
552	CREATE POLICY "{table}_delete" ON public.{table_name}
553	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
554	
555	-- Index foreign keys
556	CREATE INDEX idx_{table}_user_id ON public.{table_name}(user_id);
557	
558	-- Auto-update timestamp trigger
559	CREATE TRIGGER set_{table}_updated_at
560	  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.{table_name}
561	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at();
562	```
563	
564	### Enum Pattern (use CHECK constraint, not Postgres ENUM)
565	```sql
566	-- ❌ AVOID: Postgres ENUM (can't remove values, migration nightmare)
567	CREATE TYPE project_status AS ENUM ('active', 'archived');
568	
569	-- ✅ USE: CHECK constraint (easy to modify)
570	CREATE TABLE projects (
571	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
572	    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'archived', 'deleted'))
573	);
574	```
575	
576	### JSONB for Flexible Data
577	```sql
578	-- Use JSONB for user preferences, metadata, settings
579	ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN preferences jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;
580	
581	-- Query JSONB
582	SELECT * FROM profiles WHERE preferences->>'theme' = 'dark';
583	SELECT * FROM profiles WHERE preferences @> '{"notifications": true}';
584	
585	-- Index JSONB (GIN for containment queries)
586	CREATE INDEX idx_profiles_preferences ON profiles USING GIN (preferences);
587	```
588	
589	### Subscription/Billing Tables
590	```sql
591	CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
592	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
593	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
594	  plan text NOT NULL CHECK (plan IN ('free', 'pro', 'team')),
595	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
596	    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'past_due', 'canceled', 'trialing')),
597	  external_id text, -- Dodo payment ID or Shopify subscription ID
598	  current_period_start timestamptz,
599	  current_period_end timestamptz,
600	  cancel_at_period_end boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
601	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
602	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
603	);

605	ALTER TABLE subscriptions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
606	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own_sub" ON subscriptions
607	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
608	-- Only service role can INSERT/UPDATE (from webhook handler)
609	CREATE POLICY "service_manage_subs" ON subscriptions
610	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
611	```

613	---
614	
615	## 8. BACKUP & DISASTER RECOVERY
616	
617	### Supabase Managed Backups
618	- **Pro plan:** Daily backups, 7-day retention
619	- **Team plan:** Daily backups, 14-day retention
620	- **Enterprise:** Point-in-time recovery (PITR), 30-day retention
621	
622	### Manual Backup (before risky migrations)
623	```bash
624	# Dump full database
625	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --no-owner > backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump
626	
627	# Dump specific table
628	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --table=public.projects > projects_backup.dump
629	
630	# Restore from backup
631	pg_restore --dbname=$DATABASE_URL --no-owner --clean backup.dump
632	```
633	
634	### Pre-Migration Safety Script
635	```bash
636	#!/usr/bin/env bash
637	set -euo pipefail
638	# Run BEFORE any risky migration
639	
640	echo "Creating pre-migration backup..."
641	pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" --format=custom --no-owner > "backup_pre_migration_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump"
642	echo "Backup complete: $(ls -lh backup_pre_migration_*.dump | tail -1)"
643	
644	echo "Checking current migration state..."
645	psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT version, name FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;"
646	
647	echo "Ready to apply migration. Backup is saved."
648	```

651	
652	## 9. TYPE GENERATION WORKFLOW
653	
654	```bash
655	# From local Supabase (development)
656	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --local > lib/supabase/types.ts
657	
658	# From remote Supabase (staging/production)
659	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --project-ref $SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF > lib/supabase/types.ts
660	
661	# Verify types compile
662	pnpm tsc --noEmit
663	```
664	
665	### Using Generated Types
666	```ts
667	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
668	
669	// Table row type
670	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
671	
672	// Insert type (omits auto-generated fields)
673	type ProjectInsert = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Insert']
674	
675	// Update type (all fields optional)
676	type ProjectUpdate = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Update']
677	
678	// Use in Supabase queries for type safety
679	const { data } = await supabase
680	  .from('projects')
681	  .select('id, name, status')
682	  .returns<Pick<Project, 'id' | 'name' | 'status'>[]>()
683	```
684	
685	**Rule: Regenerate types after EVERY schema change. If TypeScript complains about a column that exists in the database, the types file is stale.**
686	
687	---
688	
689	## 10. CONNECTION MANAGEMENT
690	
691	### Supabase Connection Pooling
692	Supabase uses PgBouncer (Supavisor) for connection pooling:
693	- **Port 5432:** Direct connection (limited connections, use for migrations only)
694	- **Port 6543:** Pooled connection (use for application queries)
695	
696	```
697	# .env
698	# For application (pooled)
699	DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres
700	
701	# For migrations (direct)
702	DIRECT_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
703	```
704	
705	### Connection Limits
706	- **Free:** 60 direct + unlimited pooled
707	- **Pro:** 100 direct + unlimited pooled
708	- **Team:** 200 direct + unlimited pooled
709	
710	If hitting limits: reduce connection pool in application code, use pooled connection URL, close connections after use.
711	
712	---
713	
714	## 11. DEBUGGING DATABASE ISSUES
715	
716	### Empty Query Results (90% of the time: RLS)
717	```sql
718	-- Check if RLS is blocking
719	SET request.jwt.claims = '{"sub": "user-uuid"}';
720	SET role = 'authenticated';
721	SELECT * FROM projects; -- Does this return rows?
722	RESET role;
723	RESET request.jwt.claims;
724	```
725	
726	### Slow Queries
727	```sql
728	-- Find slow queries
729	SELECT query, calls, mean_exec_time, total_exec_time
730	FROM pg_stat_statements
731	ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
732	LIMIT 10;
733	
734	-- Check missing indexes
735	SELECT
736	  relname AS table,
737	  seq_scan, seq_tup_read,
738	  idx_scan, idx_tup_fetch,
739	  CASE WHEN seq_scan > 0
740	    THEN ROUND(seq_tup_read::numeric / seq_scan, 0)
741	    ELSE 0
742	  END AS avg_rows_per_seq_scan
743	FROM pg_stat_user_tables
744	WHERE seq_scan > 100
745	ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC;
746	-- High seq_tup_read + low idx_scan = missing index
747	```
748	
749	### Lock Contention
750	```sql
751	-- Check active locks
752	SELECT pid, mode, relation::regclass, granted
753	FROM pg_locks
754	WHERE NOT granted;
755	
756	-- Kill a blocking query (use with caution)
757	SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);
758	-- Or force: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid);
759	```
760	
761	### Database Size Monitoring
762	```sql
763	-- Total database size
764	SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database()));
765	
766	-- Size per table
767	SELECT
768	  tablename,
769	  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS total,
770	  pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS data,
771	  pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size('public.' || tablename)) AS indexes
772	FROM pg_tables
773	WHERE schemaname = 'public'
774	ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename) DESC;
775	```
776

166	SECURITY DEFINER
167	AS $$
168	DECLARE
169	  v_studio_id uuid;
170	BEGIN
171	  SELECT studio_id INTO v_studio_id
172	  FROM flash_events
173	  WHERE id = p_event_id;
174	
175	  IF NOT EXISTS (
176	    SELECT 1 FROM studio_members
177	    WHERE studio_id = v_studio_id
178	      AND user_id = auth.uid()
179	      AND deactivated_at IS NULL
180	  ) THEN
181	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'forbidden';
182	  END IF;
183	END;
184	$$;
185	
186	
187	-- ============================================================
188	-- SECTION 8 — RPC: mark_flash_slot_walkin
189	--
190	-- Called from a server action using the service-role client
191	-- (no auth.uid() available), so no membership check here.
192	-- Creates a client upsert, a bookings row, then transitions
193	-- the slot directly open → booked (skipping reserved).
194	-- Returns: { booking_id, booking_token, slot_id } or { error }
195	-- ============================================================
196	
197	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mark_flash_slot_walkin(
198	  p_slot_id        uuid,
199	  p_client_info    jsonb,    -- { first_name, last_name?, email, phone?, notes? }
200	  p_charge_at_desk boolean   -- hint for the caller; stored in booking metadata
201	)
202	RETURNS jsonb
203	LANGUAGE plpgsql
204	SECURITY DEFINER
205	AS $$
206	DECLARE
207	  v_slot          flash_event_slots%ROWTYPE;
208	  v_event         flash_events%ROWTYPE;
209	  v_client_id     uuid;
210	  v_booking_id    uuid;
211	  v_booking_token text;
212	  v_artist_id     uuid;
213	BEGIN
214	  -- Lock the slot atomically; skip if already locked by concurrent request
215	  SELECT * INTO v_slot
216	  FROM flash_event_slots
217	  WHERE id = p_slot_id
218	    AND status = 'open'
219	  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;
220	
221	  IF NOT FOUND THEN
222	    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'slot_unavailable');
223	  END IF;
224	
225	  -- Resolve parent event
226	  SELECT * INTO v_event FROM flash_events WHERE id = v_slot.flash_event_id;
227	  IF NOT FOUND THEN
228	    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'event_not_found');
229	  END IF;
230	
231	  -- Upsert client by email scoped to this studio (mirrors public_reserve_flash_slot)
232	  INSERT INTO clients (studio_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, source, created_at, updated_at)
233	  VALUES (
234	    v_event.studio_id,
235	    p_client_info->>'first_name',
236	    NULLIF(p_client_info->>'last_name', ''),
237	    LOWER(TRIM(p_client_info->>'email')),
238	    NULLIF(p_client_info->>'phone', ''),
239	    'walk-in',
240	    now(),
241	    now()
242	  )
243	  ON CONFLICT (studio_id, email) DO UPDATE
244	    SET updated_at = now()
245	  RETURNING id INTO v_client_id;
246	
247	  -- Resolve artist (event artist → first active studio artist)
248	  v_artist_id := v_event.artist_id;
249	  IF v_artist_id IS NULL THEN
250	    SELECT id INTO v_artist_id
251	    FROM artists
252	    WHERE studio_id = v_event.studio_id AND status = 'active'
253	    ORDER BY sort_order
254	    LIMIT 1;
255	  END IF;
256	
257	  IF v_artist_id IS NULL THEN
258	    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'no_artist_available');
259	  END IF;
260	
261	  -- Generate IDs
262	  v_booking_token := gen_random_uuid()::text;
263	  v_booking_id    := gen_random_uuid();
264	
265	  -- Create booking row (status=pending; payment collected at desk separately)
266	  INSERT INTO bookings (
267	    id, studio_id, client_id, artist_id,
268	    scheduled_at, duration_min,
269	    status, price_cents, deposit_cents, deposit_paid,
270	    booking_token, source,
271	    notes, client_notes,
272	    location_id, metadata,
273	    consent_required,
274	    created_at, updated_at
275	  ) VALUES (
276	    v_booking_id,
277	    v_event.studio_id,
278	    v_client_id,
279	    v_artist_id,
280	    v_slot.slot_start,
281	    (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (v_slot.slot_end - v_slot.slot_start)) / 60)::int,
282	    'pending',
283	    v_event.slot_price_cents,
284	    0,         -- walk-ins pay at desk; no online deposit
285	    false,
286	    v_booking_token,
287	    'walk-in',
288	    NULLIF(p_client_info->>'notes', ''),
289	    NULL,
290	    v_event.location_id,
291	    jsonb_build_object(
292	      'flash_event_id',   v_event.id,
293	      'flash_event_slug', v_event.slug,
294	      'walk_in',          true,
295	      'charge_at_desk',   p_charge_at_desk
296	    ),
297	    false,
298	    now(),
299	    now()
300	  );
301	
302	  -- Transition slot directly to booked (walk-in skips reserved state)
303	  UPDATE flash_event_slots
304	  SET status         = 'booked',
305	      booking_id     = v_booking_id,
306	      walk_in        = true,
307	      reserved_until = NULL,
308	      -- grace window starts from slot_start, not now()
309	      grace_expires_at = v_slot.slot_start + interval '15 minutes'
310	  WHERE id = v_slot.id;
311	
312	  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
313	    'booking_id',    v_booking_id,
314	    'booking_token', v_booking_token,
315	    'slot_id',       v_slot.id
316	  );
317	END;
318	$$;

322	-- SECTION 9 — RPC: mark_flash_slot_no_show
323	--
324	-- Staff-facing. Validates slot is 'booked' and not yet checked in.
325	-- Sets status='no_show', mirrors to the linked booking row.
326	-- Returns true if transition occurred.
327	-- ============================================================
328	
329	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mark_flash_slot_no_show(p_slot_id uuid)
330	RETURNS boolean
331	LANGUAGE plpgsql
332	SECURITY DEFINER
333	AS $$
334	DECLARE
335	  v_slot flash_event_slots%ROWTYPE;
336	BEGIN
337	  -- Membership guard: caller must be an active studio member
338	  PERFORM _flash_assert_studio_member_for_slot(p_slot_id);
339	
340	  -- Lock and validate slot state
341	  SELECT * INTO v_slot
342	  FROM flash_event_slots
343	  WHERE id = p_slot_id
344	    AND status = 'booked'
345	    AND checked_in_at IS NULL
346	  FOR UPDATE;
347	
348	  IF NOT FOUND THEN
349	    RETURN false;  -- Already no-show, not booked, or already checked in
350	  END IF;
351	
352	  -- Transition slot
353	  UPDATE flash_event_slots
354	  SET status            = 'no_show',
355	      no_show_marked_at = now()
356	  WHERE id = p_slot_id;
357	
358	  -- Mirror status to booking row so booking list reflects reality
359	  UPDATE bookings
360	  SET status     = 'no_show',
361	      updated_at = now()
362	  WHERE id = v_slot.booking_id;
363	
364	  RETURN true;
365	END;
366	$$;
367	
368	
369	-- ============================================================
370	-- SECTION 10 — RPC: mark_flash_slot_checked_in
371	--
372	-- Staff-facing. Validates slot is 'booked'. Sets checked_in_at=now().
373	-- Idempotent: calling a second time is a no-op (returns true).
374	-- ============================================================
375	
376	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mark_flash_slot_checked_in(p_slot_id uuid)
377	RETURNS boolean
378	LANGUAGE plpgsql
379	SECURITY DEFINER
380	AS $$
381	BEGIN
382	  -- Membership guard
383	  PERFORM _flash_assert_studio_member_for_slot(p_slot_id);
384	
385	  -- Only act if slot is booked (any checked_in_at state — idempotent)
386	  UPDATE flash_event_slots
387	  SET checked_in_at = COALESCE(checked_in_at, now())
388	  WHERE id = p_slot_id
389	    AND status = 'booked';
390	
391	  RETURN FOUND;
392	END;
393	$$;
394	
395	
396	-- ============================================================
397	-- SECTION 11 — RPC: duplicate_flash_event
398	--
399	-- Staff-facing. Deep-copies event + designs; skips slots.
400	-- New event: status='draft', event_date = today + 14 days,
401	-- slug appended with '-copy-<epoch>'.
402	-- ============================================================
403	
404	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION duplicate_flash_event(p_event_id uuid)
405	RETURNS uuid
406	LANGUAGE plpgsql
407	SECURITY DEFINER
408	AS $$
409	DECLARE
410	  v_src    flash_events%ROWTYPE;
411	  v_new_id uuid;
412	  v_new_slug text;
413	BEGIN
414	  -- Membership guard
415	  PERFORM _flash_assert_studio_member_for_event(p_event_id);
416	
417	  SELECT * INTO v_src FROM flash_events WHERE id = p_event_id;
418	  IF NOT FOUND THEN
419	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'flash_event not found: %', p_event_id;
420	  END IF;
421	
422	  v_new_id   := gen_random_uuid();
423	  v_new_slug := v_src.slug || '-copy-' || EXTRACT(epoch FROM now())::bigint;
424	
425	  -- Insert new event, resetting lifecycle columns
426	  INSERT INTO flash_events (
427	    id, studio_id, artist_id,
428	    title, slug, description,
429	    event_date, start_time, end_time,
430	    slot_duration_min, slot_price_cents, deposit_cents,
431	    currency, max_slots,
432	    cover_image_url, flyer_url, location_id,
433	    public, status,
434	    published_at, cancelled_at, completed_at,
435	    tips_collected_cents,
436	    created_by, created_at, updated_at
437	  ) VALUES (
438	    v_new_id,
439	    v_src.studio_id,
440	    v_src.artist_id,
441	    v_src.title || ' (Copy)',
442	    v_new_slug,
443	    v_src.description,
444	    CURRENT_DATE + 14,
445	    v_src.start_time,
446	    v_src.end_time,
447	    v_src.slot_duration_min,
448	    v_src.slot_price_cents,
449	    v_src.deposit_cents,
450	    v_src.currency,
451	    v_src.max_slots,
452	    v_src.cover_image_url,
453	    v_src.flyer_url,
454	    v_src.location_id,
455	    v_src.public,
456	    'draft',         -- always starts as draft
457	    NULL,            -- published_at reset
458	    NULL,            -- cancelled_at reset
459	    NULL,            -- completed_at reset
460	    0,               -- tips reset
461	    auth.uid(),
462	    now(),
463	    now()
464	  );
465	
466	  -- Deep-copy designs (not slots — slots are regenerated via generate_flash_event_slots)
467	  INSERT INTO flash_event_designs (
468	    id, flash_event_id,
469	    title, image_url, size_description,
470	    placement_options, price_cents,
471	    display_order, sold_out, created_at
472	  )
473	  SELECT
474	    gen_random_uuid(),
475	    v_new_id,
476	    title, image_url, size_description,
477	    placement_options, price_cents,
478	    display_order, false, now()
479	  FROM flash_event_designs
480	  WHERE flash_event_id = p_event_id;
481	
482	  RETURN v_new_id;
483	END;
484	$$;
485	
486	
487	-- ============================================================
488	-- SECTION 12 — RPC: close_flash_event
489	--
490	-- Staff-facing. Marks event completed=now(), returns a summary
491	-- jsonb for the UI close-out modal.
492	-- ============================================================
493	
494	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION close_flash_event(p_event_id uuid)
495	RETURNS jsonb
496	LANGUAGE plpgsql
497	SECURITY DEFINER
498	AS $$
499	DECLARE
500	  v_event          flash_events%ROWTYPE;
501	  v_completed_cnt  int;
502	  v_no_show_cnt    int;
503	  v_slot_rev       bigint;
504	  v_deposit_rev    bigint;
505	  v_top_design_id  uuid;
506	  v_top_design_ttl text;
507	  v_top_design_cnt int;
508	BEGIN
509	  -- Membership guard
510	  PERFORM _flash_assert_studio_member_for_event(p_event_id);
511	
512	  SELECT * INTO v_event FROM flash_events WHERE id = p_event_id;
513	  IF NOT FOUND THEN
514	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'flash_event not found: %', p_event_id;
515	  END IF;
516	
517	  IF v_event.status <> 'published' THEN
518	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'event must be published to close; current status: %', v_event.status;
519	  END IF;
520	
521	  -- Transition event to completed
522	  UPDATE flash_events
523	  SET status       = 'completed',
524	      completed_at = now(),
525	      updated_at   = now()
526	  WHERE id = p_event_id;
527	
528	  -- Aggregate slot stats
529	  SELECT
530	    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'booked'),
531	    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'no_show')
532	  INTO v_completed_cnt, v_no_show_cnt
533	  FROM flash_event_slots
534	  WHERE flash_event_id = p_event_id;
535	
536	  -- Revenue: sum slot_price_cents for booked slots via their booking rows
537	  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(b.price_cents), 0)
538	  INTO v_slot_rev
539	  FROM flash_event_slots fes
540	  INNER JOIN bookings b ON b.id = fes.booking_id
541	  WHERE fes.flash_event_id = p_event_id
542	    AND fes.status = 'booked';
543	
544	  -- Deposits: sum deposit_cents for booked+deposit_paid bookings
545	  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(b.deposit_cents), 0)
546	  INTO v_deposit_rev
547	  FROM flash_event_slots fes
548	  INNER JOIN bookings b ON b.id = fes.booking_id
549	  WHERE fes.flash_event_id = p_event_id
550	    AND fes.status = 'booked'
551	    AND b.deposit_paid = true;
552	
553	  -- Top design by booking count
554	  SELECT
555	    fes.design_id,
556	    fed.title,
557	    COUNT(*) AS cnt
558	  INTO v_top_design_id, v_top_design_ttl, v_top_design_cnt
559	  FROM flash_event_slots fes
560	  INNER JOIN flash_event_designs fed ON fed.id = fes.design_id
561	  WHERE fes.flash_event_id = p_event_id
562	    AND fes.status = 'booked'
563	    AND fes.design_id IS NOT NULL
564	  GROUP BY fes.design_id, fed.title
565	  ORDER BY cnt DESC
566	  LIMIT 1;
567	
568	  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
569	    'event_id',                p_event_id,
570	    'completed_count',         v_completed_cnt,
571	    'no_show_count',           v_no_show_cnt,
572	    'slot_revenue_cents',      v_slot_rev,
573	    'deposits_collected_cents', v_deposit_rev,
574	    'tips_cents',              v_event.tips_collected_cents,
575	    'top_design',              CASE
576	                                 WHEN v_top_design_id IS NOT NULL THEN
577	                                   jsonb_build_object(
578	                                     'id',    v_top_design_id,
579	                                     'title', v_top_design_ttl,
580	                                     'count', v_top_design_cnt
581	                                   )
582	                                 ELSE NULL
583	                               END,
584	    'artist_id',               v_event.artist_id
585	  );
586	END;
587	$$;
588	
589	
590	-- ============================================================
591	-- SECTION 13 — UPDATE existing confirm_flash_slot_booking
592	--
593	-- Adds grace_expires_at = slot_start + 15 minutes when
594	-- transitioning a slot to booked. Existing callers (deposit webhook)
595	-- are unaffected — same signature, richer side-effect.
596	-- ============================================================
597	
598	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION confirm_flash_slot_booking(p_booking_id uuid)
599	RETURNS boolean
600	LANGUAGE plpgsql
601	SECURITY DEFINER
602	AS $$
603	BEGIN
604	  UPDATE flash_event_slots
605	  SET status           = 'booked',
606	      reserved_until   = NULL,
607	      -- grace window: 15 minutes from scheduled slot start
608	      grace_expires_at = slot_start + interval '15 minutes'
609	  WHERE booking_id = p_booking_id
610	    AND status IN ('open', 'reserved');
611	
612	  RETURN FOUND;
613	END;
614	$$;
615	
616	
617	-- ============================================================
618	-- SECTION 14 — Table comments
619	-- ============================================================

621	COMMENT ON COLUMN flash_events.completed_at        IS 'Set by close_flash_event() when the event day is closed out';
622	COMMENT ON COLUMN flash_events.tips_collected_cents IS 'Cash/card tips collected at the event desk, recorded at close-out';

-- Sprint 1  : Inventory v1.0 — P0 unblock (F2, F3, K11)
--
-- Changes:
--   1. studio_ink_registry — add item_id FK + index + backfill + studio guard

--
-- Rollback (run in order):
--   ALTER TABLE studio_ink_registry DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_ink_registry_item_studio;
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS fn_ink_registry_item_studio_guard() CASCADE;
--   DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_studio_ink_registry_item_id;
--   ALTER TABLE studio_ink_registry DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS item_id;
--   ALTER TABLE inventory_items DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS inventory_items_min_threshold_nonneg;
-- ============================================================================

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. Add item_id FK to studio_ink_registry
--    Nullable: REACH registry rows can exist without a matching inventory item.
--    ON DELETE SET NULL: deleting the inventory item does not delete the REACH record.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE studio_ink_registry
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS item_id uuid
    REFERENCES inventory_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

COMMENT ON COLUMN studio_ink_registry.item_id IS
  'Optional FK to inventory_items. When set, links this REACH compliance record '
  'to the inventory row so Brand/Color propagate to the Inventory Items view. '
  'Backfilled by 20260429092406_inventory_p0_fixes on LOWER(TRIM(brand+color)) match.';

-- Index: speeds up JOIN in inventory items query (category=ink filter)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_studio_ink_registry_item_id
  ON studio_ink_registry(item_id)
  WHERE item_id IS NOT NULL;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. Backfill: match on (studio_id, LOWER(TRIM(brand)), LOWER(TRIM(color)))
--    for category='ink' inventory items.
--    Only sets item_id when currently NULL (safe to re-run).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

UPDATE studio_ink_registry r
SET item_id = i.id
FROM inventory_items i
WHERE i.studio_id  = r.studio_id
  AND LOWER(TRIM(i.brand))  = LOWER(TRIM(r.brand))
  AND LOWER(TRIM(i.color))  = LOWER(TRIM(r.color))
  AND i.category             = 'ink'
  AND r.item_id              IS NULL
  -- Prefer the most recently updated item when multiple match
  AND i.id = (
    SELECT id FROM inventory_items ii
    WHERE ii.studio_id = r.studio_id
      AND LOWER(TRIM(ii.brand)) = LOWER(TRIM(r.brand))
      AND LOWER(TRIM(ii.color)) = LOWER(TRIM(r.color))
      AND ii.category = 'ink'
    ORDER BY ii.updated_at DESC
    LIMIT 1
  );

-- Diagnostic: count matched vs unmatched (viewable in Supabase SQL editor / migration log)
DO $$
DECLARE
  v_matched   int;
  v_unmatched int;
BEGIN
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_matched   FROM studio_ink_registry WHERE item_id IS NOT NULL;
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_unmatched FROM studio_ink_registry WHERE item_id IS NULL;
  RAISE NOTICE 'studio_ink_registry backfill complete — matched: %, unmatched (need manual link): %',
    v_matched, v_unmatched;
END $$;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. Cross-table studio consistency guard
--    Ensures item_id, when set, belongs to the same studio as the registry row.
--    Implemented as a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger (CHECK constraints cannot
--    reference other tables in Postgres).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_ink_registry_item_studio_guard()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.item_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM inventory_items
      WHERE id = NEW.item_id
        AND studio_id = NEW.studio_id
    ) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION
        'ink_registry_item_studio_mismatch: item_id % does not belong to studio_id %',
        NEW.item_id, NEW.studio_id
        USING ERRCODE = 'P0001';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_ink_registry_item_studio_guard ON studio_ink_registry;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_ink_registry_item_studio_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF item_id ON studio_ink_registry
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION fn_ink_registry_item_studio_guard();

COMMENT ON FUNCTION fn_ink_registry_item_studio_guard() IS
  'S1 inventory P0 — guards against linking a studio_ink_registry row '
  'to an inventory_items row from a different studio. '
  'Raises P0001/ink_registry_item_studio_mismatch on violation.';

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. RLS policy check for item_id
--    The existing studio_ink_registry RLS policies gate on studio_id.
--    item_id is an optional column pointing to inventory_items; access is already
--    covered by those policies (row is only visible if studio_id passes).
--    No additional policy needed — the FK join in queries inherits RLS from
--    inventory_items when queried directly on that table.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. min_threshold >= 0 constraint on inventory_items
--    Uses NOT VALID to skip locking re-validation of existing rows, then
--    validates separately (lighter lock on a possibly large table).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- First, fix any existing rows where min_threshold is negative (defensive)
UPDATE inventory_items
SET min_threshold = 0
WHERE min_threshold < 0;

ALTER TABLE inventory_items
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS inventory_items_min_threshold_nonneg;

ALTER TABLE inventory_items
  ADD CONSTRAINT inventory_items_min_threshold_nonneg
  CHECK (min_threshold >= 0)
  NOT VALID;

ALTER TABLE inventory_items
  VALIDATE CONSTRAINT inventory_items_min_threshold_nonneg;

-- ============================================================================
-- Migration : 20260429092407_inventory_low_stock_trigger.sql
-- Sprint 1  : Inventory v1.0 — Low stock auto-alert trigger (F3)
--
-- Creates:
--   - Partial unique index on stock_alerts (studio_id, item_id)
--     WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL — required for ON CONFLICT in trigger
--   - fn_inventory_low_stock_handler() — fires on current_stock / min_threshold change
--   - trg_inventory_low_stock        — AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE on inventory_items
--
-- Behaviour:
--   - When current_stock < min_threshold AND min_threshold > 0:
--       INSERT open alert (idempotent — skips if open alert already exists)
--   - When current_stock >= min_threshold:
--       Auto-resolve any open alert for that item (sets acknowledged_at = now())
--
-- Rollback:
--   DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_inventory_low_stock ON inventory_items;
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS fn_inventory_low_stock_handler() CASCADE;
--   DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_stock_alerts_open_per_item;
-- ============================================================================

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. Partial unique index
--    Enforces at most one open (unacknowledged) alert per (studio_id, item_id).
--    Required for the ON CONFLICT clause in fn_inventory_low_stock_handler.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_alerts_open_per_item
  ON stock_alerts(studio_id, item_id)
  WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. Low-stock handler function
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_inventory_low_stock_handler()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Skip cascaded calls from bulk imports / parent triggers
  IF pg_trigger_depth() > 1 THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.min_threshold > 0 AND NEW.current_stock < NEW.min_threshold THEN
    -- ── Open alert (idempotent) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- alert_type = 'low_stock' per existing stock_alerts schema
    -- current_stock + threshold snapshot at time of alert creation
    INSERT INTO stock_alerts (
      studio_id,
      item_id,
      alert_type,
      current_stock,
      threshold,
      created_at,
      updated_at
    )
    VALUES (
      NEW.studio_id,
      NEW.id,
      'low_stock',
      NEW.current_stock,
      NEW.min_threshold,
      now(),
      now()
    )
    ON CONFLICT (studio_id, item_id)
      WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL
    DO NOTHING;
    -- DO NOTHING: if an open alert already exists, leave it untouched.
    -- The stock snapshot on the existing row is intentionally NOT updated —
    -- the alert records the moment it first fired, not the current value.

  ELSIF NEW.current_stock >= NEW.min_threshold THEN
    -- ── Auto-resolve open alert ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Sets acknowledged_at but NOT acknowledged_by (system resolution, no user)
    -- stock_alerts has no notes column — resolution is signalled by acknowledged_at alone
    UPDATE stock_alerts
    SET acknowledged_at = now(),
        updated_at      = now()
    WHERE item_id         = NEW.id
      AND acknowledged_at IS NULL;

  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION fn_inventory_low_stock_handler() IS
  'S1 inventory — auto-creates stock_alerts row when current_stock drops below '
  'min_threshold (min > 0 guard). Auto-resolves open alerts when stock returns '
  'at or above threshold. Throttled: skips when pg_trigger_depth() > 1 to '
  'prevent cascade floods from bulk imports or parent triggers.';

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. Trigger
--    AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF current_stock, min_threshold
--    Column-level specificity avoids firing on unrelated UPDATE columns.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_inventory_low_stock ON inventory_items;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_inventory_low_stock
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF current_stock, min_threshold
  ON inventory_items
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION fn_inventory_low_stock_handler();

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. Backfill: open alerts for existing items already below threshold
--    Runs once as part of migration; idempotent (only inserts where none exist).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

INSERT INTO stock_alerts (
  studio_id,
  item_id,
  alert_type,
  current_stock,
  threshold,
  created_at,
  updated_at
)
SELECT
  i.studio_id,
  i.id,
  'low_stock',
  i.current_stock,
  i.min_threshold,
  now(),
  now()
FROM inventory_items i
WHERE i.min_threshold > 0
  AND i.current_stock < i.min_threshold
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM stock_alerts sa
    WHERE sa.item_id = i.id
      AND sa.acknowledged_at IS NULL
  );

DO $$
DECLARE v_backfilled int;
BEGIN
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_backfilled
  FROM stock_alerts
  WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL
    AND created_at >= now() - interval '5 seconds';
  RAISE NOTICE 'Low-stock backfill: % open alerts created for pre-existing below-threshold items.',
    v_backfilled;
END $$;
